sources.entry: ZITADEL | Identity infrastructure with multi-tenancy, SSO and passkeys

summary.one_liner: ZITADEL is an open-source, API-first identity and access management platform offering SSO, MFA, passkeys, OIDC/SAML, SCIM and multi-tenant organizations, available self-hosted or as a SaaS cloud.
summary.what_it_does: ZITADEL provides authentication and identity management, including single sign-on, username/password login, passkeys (FIDO2/WebAuthn), MFA (OTP, U2F, email and SMS OTP), LDAP, enterprise and social identity providers, OpenID Connect, SAML 2.0 and device authorization. It supports machine-to-machine auth via JWT Profile, PAT and client credentials, plus token exchange and impersonation. Its multi-tenancy model runs Identity System, then Organizations, then Projects, with B2B onboarding, delegated role management and domain discovery. Every resource is exposed through gRPC, connectRPC and REST/HTTP JSON APIs, and each mutation is written as an event that can be audited or streamed out via webhooks. Self-hosting is done with Docker Compose or Kubernetes, and the README names PostgreSQL (14 or later) as the database.
use_cases: add single sign-on to a SaaS product
OIDC or SAML integration for applications
notable: Event-sourced audit trail: every mutation stored as an immutable event, streamable via webhooks
Strict multi-tenant hierarchy: Instances, Organizations, Projects
API-first with gRPC, connectRPC and REST for every resource
Same codebase for ZITADEL Cloud and self-hosted deployments
Zero-downtime updates without external session stores
caveats: Requires PostgreSQL 14 or later as a database dependency
Production self-hosting needs Docker Compose or Kubernetes setup; professional support is offered separately
Cloud SaaS uses pay-as-you-go pricing after a free start
